newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex gains escalate in pre-close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex gains escalate in pre-close.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices made a session high near the market's close Thursday, sharpening gains in crude oil and heating oil which were following gasoline's lead, traders said.
"It opened pretty bearish, and shorts were caught by surprise when prices went up," said a trader, citing short covering as contributing to the oil complex's rise overall.

October unleaded gasoline made a session high of 64.50 cents a gallon, rising 1.54 cents. The American Petroleum Institute's weekly inventory data showed higher-than-expected draws on gasoline, fueling bullish sentiment.
October heating oil made a session high of 65.40 cents a gallon, rising 1.19 cents.
Although API said distillate stocks built 3.24 million barrels for the week ended August 30, traders said heating oil stocks were still seasonally low.
October crude stood 20 cents higher at $23.44 a barrel.

Crude's gains lagged gasoline's as players sold crude and bought gasoline after the gasoline-to-crude crack spread had narrowed enough in the past weeks to make gasoline a buying opportunity, traders said. The October gasoline-to-crude crack widened to $3.60 a barrel from $3.20 Wednesday.
